content.text: {"primary_meaning":"The way of salvation and life with God, centered in Jesus Christ: Christ is the way to the Father, and following “the way” means trusting him and living as his disciple.","primary_basis":["John 14:6 — Jesus declares, “I am the way, and the truth, and the life”; access to the Father is through him.","Matthew 7:13–14 — the narrow way leads to life, contrasted with the broad way leading to destruction.","Hebrews 10:19–20 — Christ opens a “new and living way” into God’s presence.","Acts 9:2; 19:9, 23; 22:4; 24:14, 22 — “the Way” functions as an early designation for the Christian faith and movement.","Psalm 1:1–6 — the way of the righteous is contrasted with the way of the wicked."],"alternatives":[{"meaning":"A person’s manner of life or moral course, especially the path of righteousness and obedience as opposed to wickedness.","basis":["Psalm 1:1–6","Proverbs 4:10–19","Proverbs 14:12","Matthew 7:13–14"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"God’s revealed instruction or commandments—the divinely prescribed path, often associated with Torah and wisdom.","basis":["Deuteronomy 5:32–33","Psalm 25:4–10","Psalm 119:1–3, 30–32","Proverbs 3:5–6"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"The Christian community or movement itself, rather than primarily a symbol for an individual’s spiritual path.","basis":["Acts 9:2","Acts 19:9, 23","Acts 22:4","Acts 24:14, 22"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"The two contrasting destinies available to humanity: the way of life and the way of death.","basis":["Deuteronomy 30:15–20","Psalm 1:6","Jeremiah 21:8","Matthew 7:13–14"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"A prepared route for the coming or manifestation of the Lord, especially in prophetic and messianic texts.","basis":["Isaiah 40:3–5","Malachi 3:1","Matthew 3:3","Mark 1:2–3"],"prominence":"minority"},{"meaning":"The spiritual journey or pilgrimage of believers through the present life toward holiness and final communion with God.","basis":["Psalm 84:5–7","Isaiah 35:8–10","Luke 9:23","Hebrews 11:13–16"],"prominence":"minority"}],"has_settled_consensus":true,"confidence":"high","notes":"Christian interpretation broadly agrees that “the way” signifies the path to God, salvation, and faithful life, with Jesus as its decisive center in New Testament teaching. The precise emphasis remains context-dependent: some passages mean conduct, divine instruction, destiny, or the historical Christian movement rather than functioning as a single fixed symbol."}
